chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said when he entered the graveyards,

"O inhabitants of the dust, and O inhabitants of estrangement! As for the houses, they have been inhabited; and as for the spouses, they have been married off; and as for the wealth, it has been divided. This is the news from our side, and if only I knew what news you have."
Then he turned to his companions and said: "If they were permitted to respond, they would say, 'Indeed, the best provision is taqwā (God-consciousness).'

key_terms.أَهْلُ التُّرْبَةِ: Inhabitants of the dust/earth (address to the dead)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْغُرْبَةِ: Inhabitants of estrangement (address to the dead)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to the dead in the graveyard regarding their worldly possessions and spiritual provision?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) profound engagement with the reality of death, contrasting the transient material world with the eternal spiritual state of the deceased. By invoking the concept of *Taqwa* as the ultimate provision, the Imam underscores a key Shia theological principle: that true wealth lies in piety rather than inherited assets, a theme deeply resonant with the practice of *Ziyarat* (visiting graves) as a means of spiritual reflection and preparation for the Hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.535 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) entered the graveyard, He said:
"O’ inhabitants of the earth and estranged ones! As for your homes, they have been inhabited; As for your spouses, they have remarried; And as for your wealth, it has been divided. This is the news from our side ; if only I knew what news you have."
Then he turned to his companions and said:
"If they were permitted to respond, they would say, 'Indeed, the best provision is taqwā (God-consciousness).'"
